sources.title: Lilly FY2025 Form 10-K
sources.supports: Annual financials, R&D and debt context

sources.title: TuneLab launch
sources.supports: AI model asset and internal use

financial_anchor.caveat: Reported scale proxy amid rapid GLP-1 growth and acquired IPR&D

ai_claim.claim: TuneLab gives internal and partner scientists access to models trained on Lilly experimental data; Lilly also deployed an owned AI factory.
ai_claim.limitation: No prospective matched clinical-transition or risk-adjusted output result

strongest_counterevidence.claim: No disclosed Lilly AI-originated cohort establishes better Phase II/III transition or approval; current earnings growth is overwhelmingly marketed GLP-1 volume.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Absence of public evidence is not proof of no internal benefit

rights_limit: Lilly controls selected experiments/models, while patient, partner and licensed data remain consent- and contract-bound; federated access does not establish pooled feedback rights.
materiality_summary: 5% of FY2025 operating income is $1.315bn pre-tax annually. Programme NPV must be annuitized and tax-aligned; public evidence cannot bridge it.

arithmetic.inputs: $2.0bn assumed after-tax incremental NPV; 5 years; 8%; $1.315bn pre-tax hurdle; 18% assumed tax
arithmetic.result: $0.501bn equivalent annual benefit versus $1.078bn after-tax annual hurdle; illustrative and unproven

g2_provisional: Not passed: deployment evidence exists, but prospective quality-adjusted clinical productivity and material capture are unproven.
unresolved_questions: Which programmes were AI-assisted ex ante?
What transition rates and validation costs result?
